text:
sophie-support: Customer reports intermittent 401 when running `go get` for our Go SDK tag v1.2.3. They say sometimes it works, other times it fails in their CI. Pasting their repro and outputs below.

alice-customer: 
```
$ GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v1.2.3
go: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v1.2.3: reading https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/@v/v1.2.3.info: 401 Unauthorized

$ go env
GO111MODULE=\"\"
GOARCH=\"amd64\"
GOBIN=\"\"
GOCACHE=\"/home/user/.cache/go-build\"
GOPATH=\"/home/user/go\"
GOMODCACHE=\"/home/user/go/pkg/mod\"
GOPROXY=\"https://proxy.golang.org,direct\"
GOPRIVATE=\"\"
```

sophie-support: Thanks. Can you confirm if your repo is public or under a private org? Also any GOPRIVATE or CI-injected git tokens?

alice-customer: Repo is public under a customer org. No GOPRIVATE set in their local dev, but their CI does inject a GIT_TOKEN for private dependencies in other jobs.

tim-dev: Two quick angles: 1) If `GOPROXY=direct` succeeds, the problem is likely goproxy or how auth headers are getting forwarded. 2) Intermittent 401 could be token rotation or an env leakage in CI where a token is present sometimes and the proxy treats it as auth-required. Ask them to try `GOPROXY=direct` and `curl` the proxy URL shown in the error.

alice-customer: Tried `GOPROXY=direct` and it succeeded: 
```
$ GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v1.2.3
# success, module downloaded
```

javier-engr: If direct works but proxy fails, we'll need the raw `curl -v` to the proxy path and the response headers. Also collect the CI job environment dump (redact secrets) and the job timestamps so we can correlate with proxy logs.

alice-customer: Provided `curl -v https://proxy.golang.org/github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/@v/v1.2.3.info` output. Proxy response includes header `X-Proxy-Auth-Needed: true` and HTTP/1.1 401 at 2024-05-02T15:12:11Z. They included job id and IP.

ci-bot: Created INF-8723 and attached provided curl output, job id, and timestamp; assigned to javier-engr.

javier-engr: Opening internal trace. Hypothesis: proxy attempted to fetch tag metadata from upstream; upstream landing page triggered an auth redirect (maybe due to a webhook or DDoS protection), proxy observed a 401 and passed that back. Also consider signed annotated tags or special tag redirects that make the fetch require conditional requests. I'll correlate the provided IP and time with our proxy logs.

sophie-support: Recommended temporary mitigation to the customer: set `GOPROXY=direct` in their CI for the job that fetches this module, or use `GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct` so direct is fallback. Also advised ensuring no stray GIT_TOKEN or other auth env variables are injected into the job that fetches public modules.

alice-customer: Accepted workaround for now and will apply the `GOPROXY=direct` change. Asked us to keep them posted.

javier-engr: I'll post log correlation updates in INF-8723. If we confirm proxy-side misclassification, mitigation could be clearing the proxy cache for that module/version or adjusting how we treat upstream redirects for tags.

sophie-support: Marking thread escalated until internal triage completes. Will update customer once INF-8723 has root cause. :thumbsup:
